title: Altitude scope mismatch — strong Senior PM; target is Principal

assessment.general_capability: Product management ownership — personally owning product strategy, roadmap, and prioritization for a product at material scope with measurable outcomes. Assessed independently of target seniority.
assessment.target_specific_requirement: Principal PM Developer Platform — multi-year cross-organizational product strategy, portfolio-level scope, and executive influence over strategic bets beyond a single product.

seed_gap.gap_description: Resume shows strong Senior PM execution owning strategy and roadmap for a single developer-tools product. Target Principal role requires multi-year cross-org strategy, portfolio-level scope, and executive influence across adjacent teams.
seed_gap.recommended_fix: Probe for multi-year strategic direction, cross-organizational scope, and executive influence over strategic bets.

seed_analysis.positioning_summary: Clear Senior-level product strategy ownership for Rowan Studio. For a Principal target the question is whether the candidate's strategic scope extended beyond their single product and shaped broader portfolio or organizational direction.

related_signals.rationale: Owns strategy and roadmap for Rowan Studio with measurable outcomes.
Scope is a single product; multi-year cross-org strategy not surfaced.

persona.fallback_answer: I can speak to Studio specifically — what dimension would you like me to go deeper on?

answer_rules.answer: I own product strategy, the 2-year roadmap, and quarterly prioritization for Rowan Studio. I decide what we build, what we don't, and how we sequence launches.
Rowan Studio has 85k+ developers across mid-market software teams. My pod is 10 engineers, 2 designers, 1 researcher. Scope is Studio specifically; other Rowan products have their own PMs.
Weekly active developers tripled over three years and activation improved 28%. Five major launches, each with pre-registered success criteria I owned.

To be straightforward — I haven't shaped strategy beyond Rowan Studio. Adjacent PMs run their own roadmaps and I collaborate at launch coordination time, but I don't set direction for Rowan Build Agent or Rowan Insights. That cross-product portfolio call sits with our Director and VP.

I own a 2-year Studio roadmap but I'm not driving a multi-year portfolio bet or an org-wide product-platform direction. That's the Director's and VP's work. I feed into their thinking but I don't own it.
I present Studio roadmap and performance to the VP of Product monthly. I don't influence strategic bets outside Studio or sit in exec staff decisions. I'm not driving org-wide investment calls.
I'd be candid — I operate at a strong Senior level on Studio specifically. I haven't operated at Principal altitude across a portfolio or org-wide platform. That's a stretch for me today.
